title: Torlando
summary: Chapter 9 is a two-hour ensemble account of employment, Comic-Con, public exposure, sexualized ‘games,’ creative apprenticeship and a Pure Recreation Crew road trip. It begins with a stable ‘Keep that fire alive’ refrain whose performer and formal title still require recording verification. Steve Lee then presents reasons to keep him after a two-month trial away from Fat Sal's. His list—show up promptly, contribute to Mangchi, improve performance readiness and share ideas—is meaningful evidence of agency. Yet it includes stopping sleeping pills, which is not safe individualized advice, and the discussion occurs inside a sharp power imbalance: David funds the work, announces the last paycheck and decides whether Steve returns to his old job. The episode immediately tests whether gratitude and belonging create sexual permission. Steve admits touching David's genitals while David slept, calls it fun or bonding, and offers to stop. Later reconstruction establishes that contact began before the recipient could consent, a direct ‘No, what are you doing?’ followed, and the room calls it ‘highly inappropriate.’ David admits fabricating part of his retelling, so gesture and dialogue details remain disputed without erasing the core admitted contact. Sexual orientation jokes are irrelevant to consent. Gratitude is also not permission: Steve repeatedly says he does not literally want anal sex even while using a ten-second offer as an exaggerated measure of what David's gifts and travel meant to him. His retraction controls. The Macau recap protects private sex workers and keeps costs, service codes and sexual histories as speaker claims. ‘Chinese Ellen Page’ is a comparison, not an identity, and the historical name in the speech is not silently modernized as a quotation. Korean oppa is corrected as a context-dependent address for an older male, not simply uncle or porn language. Poon's attachment to Macau and intimacy remains distinct from the room's transactional framing. The chicken, Hinge, steamroller and Funky Worm games repeatedly escalate touch. Some participants state rules, participate and say chicken; elsewhere people invent one ‘free pass’ for Critter or skip incremental steps. Third parties cannot grant Critter's consent, one encounter does not authorize the next, and a game is not an instruction for listeners. Public-space conduct beside sleeping passengers and unauthorized Comic-Con access remain admitted conduct, not operational advice. David's Comic-Con history carries one of the episode's strongest creative lines. He recalls arriving a month early, turning the mistake into a Mexico trip, meeting Eric Nakamura and Martin Wong, drawing Martin Yan for Giant Robot issue 9 overnight, and learning booth sales by standing and engaging. The Oakland Museum of California's Giant Robot curriculum independently corroborates the Martin Yan assignment and issue number; Giant Robot's store verifies issue 9. This grounds a real apprenticeship sequence: ask for work, deliver immediately, become useful, then learn direct audience contact. His body-size and hygiene generalizations about convention attendees remain dehumanizing opinions, and flexibility cannot test HIV. A private woman's body photo and speculative diagnosis are not publishable archive objects. The 2014 event chain is externally anchored. Reporting identifies Kirk Von Hammett's Fear FestEvil After Party on July 25 during San Diego Comic-Con, with Kirk Hammett and Exodus and Scion Audio Visual involvement. The episode says Prince Paul interviewed Steve about the Kwangou/Kwangu album nearby. The unrecovered raw interview is a high-priority source lead because the room says the commercial edit would omit much of the explicit exchange. Prince Paul's works are repaired to Handsome Boy Modeling School, A Prince Among Thieves, De La Soul Is Dead, 3 Feet High and Rising and Gravediggaz. Richard Christy's surname and Charred Walls of the Damned are repaired, as are the Stern staff names. David's official Howard Stern page independently confirms his February 7, 2012 appearance and green-room mural. His argument that Stern inspired DVDASA is therefore anchored, while his claims about staff relationships, Howard's private interests and a future succession remain attributed admiration and ambition. The creative thesis is preserved rather than endorsed wholesale: heart and expression matter more to David than spelling, grammar or technique; literal podcast speech and subjective art operate differently; impatience to master a medium can energize or distort the work. The same section also supplies an important consent limit: David says several former collaborators did not want the public life he imagined, one person reportedly suffered job consequences, and being ‘un-blackmailable’ describes David and Asa, not everyone around them. Bobby Lee's concern for Steve's permanent image is treated as a legitimate exposure question even when David calls it jealousy. Poon's separate Comic-Con day with a private companion shows why. She asks for one-on-one lunch, Poon avoids calling the cast partly because he fears being pulled into a recorded show, and their prior sexual history does not create present consent. Her household, residence, relationship secrecy and travel trail stay private. The Mexico section preserves the trip's sex-work account, contemptuous language, condom use, stopped penetration, handwashing warnings and reported paid acts. It does not diagnose workers. CDC guidance says bacterial vaginosis is a treatable bacterial imbalance that may be asymptomatic or involve discharge, pain, itching, burning or a fish-like odor, and diagnosis requires clinical evaluation/testing. Smell alone cannot establish BV, the phrase ‘bacterial vegetables’ is wrong, and BV is not simply shorthand for every STI or sanitation claim. Private workers' scars, bodies and alleged health conditions stay out of neutral discovery. The road trip ends with Manzanilla, sold-out hotels, Hotel del Coronado, pool games and competing sandcastles. The group discusses kicking a professional sculpture but builds its own; the tide, not the group, destroys it. Critter's decision to sit out swimming is restored with his stated reasons—no swimwear, cost and heat—rather than flattened into refusal to have fun. Poon's response to a couple at the beach returns to the episode's emotional question: everyone may want love, but not everyone wants a relationship, and wanting affection while wanting the other person to leave is a contradiction the room identifies rather than solves. Trivia is abandoned in extreme heat. The ending includes physical escalation, a request not to fight and a direct neck-pain report, followed by decoder artifacts and rough Mangchi lyrics. All difficult ideas remain in the source layer. The editorial layer labels provenance, privacy, consent, medical uncertainty and unsafe conduct; it does not censor viewpoints. No named line-level dialogue publishes because there are zero held-out identity windows and zero validated turns.

connections.note: The two-month return option and rehire list make the friendship-employment power structure explicit.
Performance readiness, costume work and the Scion interview join the band's creative-production timeline.
The episode admits contact began while David was asleep and later supplies a direct refusal and an explicit inappropriate judgment.
A ten-second sexual offer is framed as gratitude for travel and clothes, then repeatedly retracted as nonliteral and unwanted.
Paid-sex memories and the Poon/Steve bond continue, while private workers and secondhand details remain restricted.
The Martin Yan assignment and booth work document David's shift from asking for a first job to learning audience-facing salesmanship.
A long personal history connects zines, Giant Robot, corporate expansion, unauthorized access and public recognition.
The July 25, 2014 Scion event anchors the episode and the Prince Paul interview chronology.
Steve's detailed discography recall shows an interviewee first honoring the interviewer as a creative influence.
David identifies his 2012 Stern appearance as a direct model for DVDASA's long-form candor.
David argues heart matters more than polish while distinguishing literal broadcast speech from subjective art.
Former collaborators, Steve's brother and Poon's companion expose the limits of David and Asa's un-blackmailable philosophy.
A private former teammate's body becomes a racialized recruiting spectacle and episode title without proven publication consent.
The no-snitching game is tested against Steve identifying David to Comic-Con security under pressure.
CDC evidence corrects the cast's odor-only diagnosis and false single-symptom claim.
ATVs, food, pool games and sandcastles become an alternative to the group's transactional-sex travel structure.
The group resists destroying another person's sculpture, builds its own and watches the tide erase it.
Costumes, physical games, a private body photo, Comic-Con footage, sandcastles and the overheated ending all require video.

speaker_policy: Public episode context may identify David Choe, Asa Akira, Steve Lee/Stevie Weeby, Bill Poon, Critter Fleming, Val/Valentin, Bobby Trivia, Saelee Oh and the public figures discussed at scene level. source_notes: The cleaner records 70 edits—37 empty artifacts and 33 degenerate-run edits—and reduces 3,473 raw segments to 3,419 clean segments. It removes about 19 words while consolidating repeated decoder material.
The opening refrain is stable, but the performer and formal song title remain unresolved; the closing Mangchi lyrics and decoder tail are not quotation-grade.

The Oakland Museum of California's Giant Robot curriculum independently states that Martin Wong asked David Choe for a Martin Yan illustration and that he delivered it for issue 9: https://museumca.org/wp-content/uploads/2014/06/curriculum_Giant-Robot-Curriculum-2014.pdf
Giant Robot's official store independently verifies issue 9: https://www.giantrobot.com/products/giant-robot-issue-9

Contemporaneous event reporting identifies the free July 25, 2014 Kirk Von Hammett's Fear FestEvil After Party during San Diego Comic-Con, involving Scion Audio Visual, Kirk Hammett and Exodus: https://loudwire.com/metallica-kirk-hammett-exodus-fear-festevil-show-comic-con/

Howard Stern's official site verifies David Choe's February 7, 2012 interview and green-room tribute mural, grounding the episode's claimed format influence: https://www.howardstern.com/show/2012/02/07/david-choe-super-artist-rundowngallerymodel-1073/

CDC guidance says BV may be asymptomatic or produce several symptoms and requires healthcare evaluation/testing. Odor alone does not diagnose a private worker: https://www.cdc.gov/bacterial-vaginosis/about/index.html
The Prince Paul/Stevie Weeby raw interview, Jim Lee Stern poster, exact Kwangou/Kwangu catalog spelling and Kevin Hayes identity remain source leads, not verified facts.
At 3184, ‘I will do it again’ is contextually likely missing ‘not’; retain as an audio-verification candidate rather than silently changing the source.
At 7331, ‘don't show my heart’ likely refers to an erection, but video/audio must resolve the wording.
Zero held-out identity windows and zero validated turns means no line-level speaker names.
